jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
jobs.description:
About the Organization
Imagine you are walking past a shallow pond. A small child is drowning in it. You could wade in and save her — at no risk to yourself, at the cost of nothing more than muddy clothes. Do you have an obligation to act?

Most people say yes, without hesitation.

Peter Singer's next question is harder: if that is true, what ought you to do about the thousands of children who die every day from causes that are equally preventable, equally treatable, and equally real — just farther away?

That question is the founding idea of The Life You Can Save (TLYCS). Since Singer published his book of that name in 2009, TLYCS has grown into a global organization that translates moral argument into measurable action: identifying the nonprofit organizations whose work has been most rigorously demonstrated to save and improve lives in some of the world’s poorest countries, and inspiring donors worldwide to support them. Over 150,000 people have encountered this argument through the book alone. Many more have engaged with it online. And more than a hundred million dollars have flowed to extraordinarily effective organizations as a result.
We are now looking for the leader who will take TLYCS through its next chapter.

Role Summary
The CEO is the senior leader of TLYCS, reporting directly to the Board of Directors and responsible for the organization's strategy, culture, operations, and growth.
This is not a steady-state leadership role. We are looking for a builder
— someone who will look at what TLYCS has achieved and ask how to multiply it. The organization currently moves approximately $24 million annually to some of the most effective poverty-relief work in the world. The CEO's central charge is to grow that number, significantly and sustainably, while maintaining the intellectual rigor and donor trust that make TLYCS's recommendations credible.
Key Responsibilities
Set the direction.
Working closely with the Board, you will shape and execute TLYCS's long-term strategy — identifying where the organization can have the greatest leverage, translating strategic goals into clear priorities, and ensuring every decision stays anchored to the mission.
Own the growth agenda.
Fundraising is the engine of TLYCS's impact. You will take personal ownership of major donor relationships, lead the development team's efforts, and bring the ambition and skill to substantially expand the organization's impact. This includes both growing the funds directed to our recommended charities and securing the operational funding needed to sustain and grow TLYCS itself.
Control the resources.
Subject to the approval of the Board of Directors, you will determine how TLYCS's budget is sized and allocated, making the hard choices that keep a lean, high-performing organization effective.
Lead the team.
You will manage a senior leadership team spanning marketing, operations, and fundraising, and foster the kind of remote-first culture — high-trust, mission-driven, globally distributed — that draws exceptional people to work that matters.
Carry the flag.
You will be a principal public voice for TLYCS: with donors, with the media, with partners in the effective altruism and broader philanthropic communities, and with anyone who needs to hear a compelling case for evidence-based giving.
Essential Qualifications
We expect competitive candidates to meet all
of the following requirements:
Demonstrated commitment to TLYCS’s mission and values.
You will have a meaningful track record of acting on values aligned with TLYCS’s mission, demonstrated through your professional work, philanthropy, volunteering, advocacy or other sustained commitments. Intellectual agreement with the mission alone is not sufficient.
Experience in international development and/or global health
, including an understanding of evidence-based approaches to reducing extreme poverty and awareness of approaches used to identify high-impact, cost-effective interventions and organizations.
A demonstrated track record of nonprofit fundraising,
preferably with a focus on cultivating and securing support from major donors, foundations and/or other institutional funders, alongside an ability to spread a compelling message widely and thereby grow a broad base of individual donors.
Experience leading or overseeing marketing and communications
, including an understanding of how brand, audience engagement and compelling communications can support fundraising, organizational growth and increased giving to highly effective charities.
Several years of senior leadership experience
, with a track record of organizational growth, developing and executing strategy, building and leading high-performing teams, managing significant budgets, and earning the trust of boards and senior stakeholders.
Strong communication and external representation skills
, including the ability to communicate complex ideas with clarity and conviction to donors, partners, staff and public audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated effectiveness in a remote and globally distributed working environment
strongly preferred. 
Existing networks
among potential funders and across the philanthropy, global health and development sectors.

You are likely to be someone who combines leadership competence, intellectual seriousness and an unusually strong personal commitment to improving the lives of people living in extreme poverty.
Practical Requirements
Work environment and right to work.
This is a fully remote role. Candidates must already have the legal right to work from the country in which they will be based. TLYCS is not able to provide visa sponsorship or relocation support for this position.

Time zones and working hours.
We welcome applicants from different time zones, but this is a genuinely global role. The CEO must be able to participate regularly in internal and external meetings across TLYCS’s key markets in the United States and Australia, as well as work with team members based in South Africa. Depending on where you are based, this will require some flexibility to attend meetings outside standard working hours.

Full-time position.
This is a full-time leadership role and requires the CEO’s full professional commitment to TLYCS.
International travel.
International travel is an essential requirement of the role. Candidates should only apply if they are able and willing to travel internationally as required for Board meetings, donor engagement, team meetings, conferences and other organizational priorities.

What We Offer
A salary in the range of $150,000 USD - $225,000 USD commensurate with experience, the flexibility of fully remote work, and the knowledge that the organization you lead will, this year, direct tens of millions of dollars to people who need it most.
The Life You Can Save is an equal opportunity employer. We actively welcome applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and nationalities.
Application Instructions
To apply,
complete our short online application form . Please note that applications submitted via email or LinkedIn will not be reviewed.

Application Deadline: September 20, 2026.
Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and we may begin interviewing candidates before the application deadline.

Applications must be submitted via the application form above. 

For application-related inquiries: careers@thelifeyoucansave.org.

jobs.description:
Steamboat Creates is a community minded arts and culture organization in Northwest Colorado dedicated to strengthening our rural community through advocacy, education, cultural events, public art, and creative experiences.

The Development Director is a senior leadership position responsible for growing and diversifying revenue to support Steamboat Creates mission and long-term sustainability.

Reporting directly to the Executive Director, the Development Director will lead all fundraising strategy and execution, including major gifts, corporate sponsorships, grants, memberships, annual giving, donor stewardship, and campaign development.

This role is ideal for a highly strategic and entrepreneurial fundraiser who has successfully owned revenue goals, built fundraising systems, and cultivated meaningful donor relationships. The successful candidate will be comfortable balancing high-level strategy with hands-on execution while independently identifying opportunities, setting priorities, and driving results.

Key Responsibilities

Fundraising Strategy & Revenue Growth
Major Gifts & Donor Development
Corporate Sponsorships
Grants & Institutional Giving
Systems, Analytics & Operations
Community Engagement & Representation
Leadership & Collaboration

Qualifications

Five or more years of progressively responsible fundraising or development leadership experience.
Demonstrated success managing and achiving fundraising revenue goals.
Proven experince securing major gifts, sponsorships, grants or other significant philanthropic support.
Experience developing and managing donor pipelines and cultivation strategies.
Strong project management and organizational skills.
Excellent written, verbal and presentation skills.

Steamboat Creates offers a collaborative, mission-driven environment and the opportunity to play a leadership role in shaping the future of arts and culture in Steamboat Springs.

Horizon Underground is seeking a hands-on, field-oriented CEO to lead and grow the business through its next phase. The right candidate will combine commercial drive with practical execution; someone who respects and preserves what already works while opening new paths to growth.

Requirements

10+ years of leadership experience in infrastructure, industrial services, construction, utilities, or comparable sectors
Demonstrated track record of top-line growth: winning new customers, entering new markets, and expanding service offerings
Direct, hands-on ownership of sales and business development, including personal involvement in pursuing and closing new work
Experience expanding a services business into adjacent end markets; exposure to military, government, data center, telecom, energy, or public sector clients is particularly relevant
Demonstrated full P&L responsibility with a strong track record of revenue growth and margin expansion
Proven operational leadership experience across multi-site or regional organizations

High integrity leadership style with a strong commitment to safety and culture
Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations, business, or a related field

Experience in underground utilities, directional drilling, fiber deployment, or civil infrastructure services
Existing relationships or contracting experience in military, government, or data center construction
Familiarity with public sector procurement, bidding, and contract award processes
Background in larger corporate environments with exposure to structured operating systems, followed by leadership in smaller or founder-led businesses
Experience leading business transformation or integration initiatives
M&A experience, including acquisition integration and post-close value creation

The Program Director is responsible for the day-to-day management of the program in accordance with regulatory, contractual requirements and organizational standards.

Monitors the program effectiveness to ensure that program is achieving its goals and targets as defined by DHS.

FISCAL (If applicable)

Reviews and approves purchase requisitions and ensures that all expenditures comply with organizational procurement procedures.

FACILITIES

Collaborates with the Regional Director of Facilities/Operations in ensuring that the facilities operate in compliance with ECB, DOB, FDNY, etc. regulations.

Monitors and analyzes reports and dashboard to ensure the program meet annual program goals and targets which support the mission and vision of the organization.

Monitors DHS performance metrics and collaborates with program managerial and supervisory staff in developing strategies to ensure the program meets DHS performance metrics.

CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT (CQI)

Leads the implementation of continuous quality improvement activities.

Develops systems, process and tools which ensure the programs meet/exceed governmental/funder standards. 

Conducts program audits to ensure compliance with organizational and government/funder standards. 

Collaborates with the Senior Director of Quality Assurance and Program Development in analyzing findings from internal and external audits and establishing measures to improve the delivery of services and deficiencies.

Leads or participate in CQI projects and committees.     

ADMINISTRATIVE

Submits quality and timely reports to the organizations and other regulatory agencies as mandated to ensure the program complies with reporting requirements.

  STAFF MANAGEMENT & DEVELOPMENT

Hires, trains, coaches, and provides support to direct reports. Provides on-going performance feedback and reviews in accordance with organizational policies. 

Ensures staff receive required trainings to ensure optimal performance and delivery of service to clients.

Collaborates with Human Resources in addressing staff performance issues. 

Promotes collaboration and effective communication amongst staff and between departments through the development of interdisciplinary teams to achieve organizational goals.

  COMMUNITY RELATIONS

Establishes liaisons with appropriate community agencies to maintain linkages for services needed by the families.

Participate in local community meetings and serve as liaison with local community members and representatives.  

Minimum Qualifications

Master’s Degree in Social Worker from an accredited college/university.  

NYS licensure (LCSW or LMSW) required.

Minimum of four years human services experience with at least two years of managerial and supervisory experience with demonstrated professional progression in supervision and program management.

Experience with multi-problem families and/or individuals desirable.

Excellent analytical, evaluative, and human service management skills. 

Excellent organizational and supervisory skills. 

Excellent oral and written communication skills coupled with strong interpersonal skills.

Proficient in MS Office, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and Adobe.

OTHER REQUIREMENTS (including Physical Demands):

May be required to work long hours and a varied schedule.

Travelling throughout various locations in the New York City area.

Lifting and moving objects weighing up to 30 pounds several times a week.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Shape the Future of Finance

Pagaya is building a leading artificial intelligence network to help our partners grow their businesses and better serve their customers.

new_jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
new_jobs.description:
About the Organization
Imagine you are walking past a shallow pond. A small child is drowning in it. You could wade in and save her — at no risk to yourself, at the cost of nothing more than muddy clothes. Do you have an obligation to act?

Most people say yes, without hesitation.

Peter Singer's next question is harder: if that is true, what ought you to do about the thousands of children who die every day from causes that are equally preventable, equally treatable, and equally real — just farther away?

That question is the founding idea of The Life You Can Save (TLYCS). Since Singer published his book of that name in 2009, TLYCS has grown into a global organization that translates moral argument into measurable action: identifying the nonprofit organizations whose work has been most rigorously demonstrated to save and improve lives in some of the world’s poorest countries, and inspiring donors worldwide to support them. Over 150,000 people have encountered this argument through the book alone. Many more have engaged with it online. And more than a hundred million dollars have flowed to extraordinarily effective organizations as a result.
We are now looking for the leader who will take TLYCS through its next chapter.

Role Summary
The CEO is the senior leader of TLYCS, reporting directly to the Board of Directors and responsible for the organization's strategy, culture, operations, and growth.
This is not a steady-state leadership role. We are looking for a builder
— someone who will look at what TLYCS has achieved and ask how to multiply it. The organization currently moves approximately $24 million annually to some of the most effective poverty-relief work in the world. The CEO's central charge is to grow that number, significantly and sustainably, while maintaining the intellectual rigor and donor trust that make TLYCS's recommendations credible.
Key Responsibilities
Set the direction.
Working closely with the Board, you will shape and execute TLYCS's long-term strategy — identifying where the organization can have the greatest leverage, translating strategic goals into clear priorities, and ensuring every decision stays anchored to the mission.
Own the growth agenda.
Fundraising is the engine of TLYCS's impact. You will take personal ownership of major donor relationships, lead the development team's efforts, and bring the ambition and skill to substantially expand the organization's impact. This includes both growing the funds directed to our recommended charities and securing the operational funding needed to sustain and grow TLYCS itself.
Control the resources.
Subject to the approval of the Board of Directors, you will determine how TLYCS's budget is sized and allocated, making the hard choices that keep a lean, high-performing organization effective.
Lead the team.
You will manage a senior leadership team spanning marketing, operations, and fundraising, and foster the kind of remote-first culture — high-trust, mission-driven, globally distributed — that draws exceptional people to work that matters.
Carry the flag.
You will be a principal public voice for TLYCS: with donors, with the media, with partners in the effective altruism and broader philanthropic communities, and with anyone who needs to hear a compelling case for evidence-based giving.
Essential Qualifications
We expect competitive candidates to meet all
of the following requirements:
Demonstrated commitment to TLYCS’s mission and values.
You will have a meaningful track record of acting on values aligned with TLYCS’s mission, demonstrated through your professional work, philanthropy, volunteering, advocacy or other sustained commitments. Intellectual agreement with the mission alone is not sufficient.
Experience in international development and/or global health
, including an understanding of evidence-based approaches to reducing extreme poverty and awareness of approaches used to identify high-impact, cost-effective interventions and organizations.
A demonstrated track record of nonprofit fundraising,
preferably with a focus on cultivating and securing support from major donors, foundations and/or other institutional funders, alongside an ability to spread a compelling message widely and thereby grow a broad base of individual donors.
Experience leading or overseeing marketing and communications
, including an understanding of how brand, audience engagement and compelling communications can support fundraising, organizational growth and increased giving to highly effective charities.
Several years of senior leadership experience
, with a track record of organizational growth, developing and executing strategy, building and leading high-performing teams, managing significant budgets, and earning the trust of boards and senior stakeholders.
Strong communication and external representation skills
, including the ability to communicate complex ideas with clarity and conviction to donors, partners, staff and public audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated effectiveness in a remote and globally distributed working environment
strongly preferred. 
Existing networks
among potential funders and across the philanthropy, global health and development sectors.

You are likely to be someone who combines leadership competence, intellectual seriousness and an unusually strong personal commitment to improving the lives of people living in extreme poverty.
Practical Requirements
Work environment and right to work.
This is a fully remote role. Candidates must already have the legal right to work from the country in which they will be based. TLYCS is not able to provide visa sponsorship or relocation support for this position.

Time zones and working hours.
We welcome applicants from different time zones, but this is a genuinely global role. The CEO must be able to participate regularly in internal and external meetings across TLYCS’s key markets in the United States and Australia, as well as work with team members based in South Africa. Depending on where you are based, this will require some flexibility to attend meetings outside standard working hours.

Full-time position.
This is a full-time leadership role and requires the CEO’s full professional commitment to TLYCS.
International travel.
International travel is an essential requirement of the role. Candidates should only apply if they are able and willing to travel internationally as required for Board meetings, donor engagement, team meetings, conferences and other organizational priorities.

What We Offer
A salary in the range of $150,000 USD - $225,000 USD commensurate with experience, the flexibility of fully remote work, and the knowledge that the organization you lead will, this year, direct tens of millions of dollars to people who need it most.
The Life You Can Save is an equal opportunity employer. We actively welcome applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and nationalities.
Application Instructions
To apply,
complete our short online application form . Please note that applications submitted via email or LinkedIn will not be reviewed.

Application Deadline: September 20, 2026.
Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and we may begin interviewing candidates before the application deadline.

Applications must be submitted via the application form above. 

For application-related inquiries: careers@thelifeyoucansave.org.

new_jobs.description:
PRIMARY FUNCTION/PURPOSE

The Program Director is responsible for the day-to-day management of the program in accordance with regulatory, contractual requirements and organizational standards.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES

Monitors the program effectiveness to ensure that program is achieving its goals and targets as defined by DHS.

Manage the program multi-disciplinary teams and ensures integration of delivery of services to the families.

Ensures program staff implement procedures and policies to ensure quality service provision.  

OPERATIONS MANAGEMENT

FISCAL (If applicable)

Collaborates with Administrative Manager and/or Director of Administration in the development of annual operating budgets, reviews monthly expense reports, and ensures program expenditures are within budgeted parameters.

Ensures billing reports are submitted timely and ensures collaboration with the organizations fiscal department to ensures the Administrative Manager and/or Director of Administration responds timely to billing inquiries and request for billing corrections.

Reviews and approves purchase requisitions and ensures that all expenditures comply with organizational procurement procedures.

FACILITIES

Collaborates with the Regional Director of Facilities/Operations in ensuring that the facilities operate in compliance with ECB, DOB, FDNY, etc. regulations.

Collaborates with the Regional Director of Facilities/Operations in ensuring that program meets 95% occupancy rate.

Monitors unit work orders and complaints and ensures the operations teams respond to work orders and complaints in a timely manner.

  METRICS & PERFORMANCE

Monitors and analyzes reports and dashboard to ensure the program meet annual program goals and targets which support the mission and vision of the organization.

Monitors DHS performance metrics and collaborates with program managerial and supervisory staff in developing strategies to ensure the program meets DHS performance metrics.

CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT (CQI)

Leads the implementation of continuous quality improvement activities.

Develops systems, process and tools which ensure the programs meet/exceed governmental/funder standards. 

Conducts program audits to ensure compliance with organizational and government/funder standards. 

Collaborates with the Senior Director of Quality Assurance and Program Development in analyzing findings from internal and external audits and establishing measures to improve the delivery of services and deficiencies.

Leads or participate in CQI projects and committees.     

ADMINISTRATIVE

Submits quality and timely reports to the organizations and other regulatory agencies as mandated to ensure the program complies with reporting requirements.

  STAFF MANAGEMENT & DEVELOPMENT

Hires, trains, coaches, and provides support to direct reports. Provides on-going performance feedback and reviews in accordance with organizational policies. 

Ensures staff receive required trainings to ensure optimal performance and delivery of service to clients.

Collaborates with Human Resources in addressing staff performance issues. 

Promotes collaboration and effective communication amongst staff and between departments through the development of interdisciplinary teams to achieve organizational goals.

  COMMUNITY RELATIONS

Establishes liaisons with appropriate community agencies to maintain linkages for services needed by the families.

Participate in local community meetings and serve as liaison with local community members and representatives.  

Minimum Qualifications

Master’s Degree in Social Worker from an accredited college/university.  

NYS licensure (LCSW or LMSW) required.

Minimum of four years human services experience with at least two years of managerial and supervisory experience with demonstrated professional progression in supervision and program management.

Experience with multi-problem families and/or individuals desirable.

Excellent analytical, evaluative, and human service management skills. 

Excellent organizational and supervisory skills. 

Excellent oral and written communication skills coupled with strong interpersonal skills.

Proficient in MS Office, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and Adobe.

OTHER REQUIREMENTS (including Physical Demands):

May be required to work long hours and a varied schedule.

Travelling throughout various locations in the New York City area.

Lifting and moving objects weighing up to 30 pounds several times a week.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

new_jobs.title: Managing Director, Real Assets/Infrastructure Product Specialist
new_jobs.description:
Join Hamilton Lane, a global leader in private markets, as we scale to meet the demands of our growing client base. Here, you’ll work with ambitious, high‑performing teams built on integrity, candor and collaboration, backed by our market-leading data and technology. We invest heavily in our people and our partners, giving you the platform to enrich lives, safeguard futures and grow your career.

What We Do

As one of the largest private markets investment firms globally, we provide innovative solutions to institutional and private wealth investors around the world, specializing in flexibility and full-spectrum access. We currently employ approximately 800 professionals operating in offices throughout North America, Europe, Asia Pacific and the Middle East, and have $1.0 trillion in assets under management and supervision, composed of $146.1 billion in discretionary assets and $871.5 billion in non-discretionary assets, as of December 31, 2025.

The Opportunity

As part of Hamilton Lane’s Global Client Solutions Team, the Real Assets/Infrastructure Product Manager / Platform Specialist is responsible for the overall management and execution of all aspects of one or more investment products and platforms, including fundraising support, product strategy, and ongoing investor relations across global markets.

In this role, you will act as a subject matter expert and primary point of contact across closed end and evergreen solutions partnering with our institutional and private wealth client solutions teams as well as working closely with Investment Teams within Infrastructure / Real Assets, Marketing, Legal, Operations, and other internal partners to drive product growth and deliver a superior investor experience. The successful candidate is highly motivated, detail-oriented, and comfortable operating in a fast-paced, deadline-driven, and often evolving environment.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Platform and Product Leadership

Serve as primary product/platform representative (closed end and evergreen products) for internal and external stakeholders, acting as the conduit between the investment team and client-facing teams.
Lead the day-to-day management of assigned products through the full product lifecycle, from fundraising and launch through investment period and maturity.
Develop and refine platform positioning, key messaging, and commercial narratives that clearly articulate the strategy, track record, and competitive differentiation of the platform.

Fundraising and Investor Relations

Oversee and coordinate fundraising efforts across assigned products (closed end and evergreen), partnering with Global Client Solutions to plan campaigns, track pipeline, and support targeted prospect coverage.
Lead or support investor/prospects meetings and calls, including preparation and delivery of materials covering portfolio analytics, case studies, performance, pipeline, and market developments.
Drive ongoing investor communication, including recurring and ad hoc updates, investor letters, reporting commentary, FAQs, and responses to complex inquiries.

Product Marketing and Content Ownership

Own or co-own marketing collateral for assigned platforms (e.g., pitchbooks, factsheets, platform decks, RFP language, due diligence materials) and ensure content is accurate, consistent, and up to date across channels.
Partner with Marketing and Product Development to execute go-to-market plans for new funds or product enhancements, including messaging documents, thought leadership, presentations, web content, and sales enablement tools.
Maintain platform-specific standard responses and data points to support efficient completion of RFPs, DDQs, and recurring questionnaires.

Product Operations and Technical Expertise

Develop and maintain a deep understanding of the structural, operational, and legal aspects of assigned products, including fund terms, cash flows, reporting requirements, and operational workflows.
Collaborate with Operations, Accounting, Legal, and Compliance to support product onboarding, ongoing governance, documentation, and process enhancements.
Monitor platform health and KPIs, providing data-driven insights on fundraising progress, investor mix, product capacity, and other commercial metrics to senior leadership.

Cross-Functional Collaboration and Strategy

Partner with Product Development and Investment leadership to evaluate new product ideas, feeder vehicles, and extensions that align with investor demand and firm strategy.
Provide market and competitive intelligence on the platform’s opportunity set, peer offerings, investor feedback, and structural trends to inform strategic decisions.
Communicate regularly with global sales, client teams, and internal stakeholders on key platform updates, helping to align messaging and priorities across regions and channels.

Leadership and Team Development

Provide day-to-day guidance and oversight to junior product team members supporting the platform, delegating tasks, reviewing deliverables, and contributing to training and development.
Serve as an escalation point for complex client requests or nuanced product questions, collaborating with senior stakeholders as needed.

Your Background Will Include

Must-Haves

Bachelor’s degree (B.A., B.S. or B.B.A.) or equivalent work experience; advanced degree (MBA and/or CFA) preferred but not required.
12-15+ years of experience in financial services, with meaningful exposure to technical product management, investor relations, investment consulting, or private markets (e.g., private equity, private credit, infrastructure, or evergreen products).
Demonstrated experience working directly with institutional or wealth clients, sales teams, and/or investment professionals in a client-facing or product-focused capacity.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to simplify complex topics and tailor messages to varied audiences (investors, senior management, sales, and partners).
Proven ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, prioritize effectively, and meet deadlines in a dynamic, fast-paced environment.
High degree of ownership, organization, and attention to detail; comfortable operating with limited oversight while collaborating across a matrixed organization.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint); strong aptitude for working with data, presentations, and reporting outputs.
Direct experience with private markets products or platforms, including commingled funds, evergreen vehicles, or customized mandates.
Familiarity with RFP/DDQ processes, investor reporting, and sales enablement tools.
Prior experience managing or mentoring junior team members and coordinating work across global teams.
Comfort presenting to senior internal stakeholders and external clients, including at conferences, investor meetings, and firm-wide events.

Travel Requirements

Approximately 50%+ domestic and international travel may be required, depending on platform coverage and client locations.

Benefits

At Hamilton Lane, our benefits philosophy is simple: to provide our employees with a competitive suite of benefits and services to help navigate through the complexities and challenges of working, living, raising a family, and eventually retiring. To do this, Hamilton Lane offers the following benefits:

Enhancing Your Physical and Emotional Health

Employees have access to healthcare coverage, mental health resources, health & fitness reimbursement program, and Wellness Rewards Program.

Developing Your Career

Tuition and certification reimbursement programs are available, along with continual education and development trainings for you to grow with Hamilton Lane.

For our communities, Hamilton Lane provides paid time off to volunteer and compensates for referring qualified candidates that join our team.

For growing family, we offer an adoption reimbursement program, paid time off for new parents and newlyweds, and provide travel support for nursing parents.

Safeguarding Your Financial Wellbeing

Hamilton Lane contributes to retirement programs and offers an employee stock purchasing plan.
